economy.summary: His campaign says he wants to build on the region's energy sector and leverage the Shell petrochemical plant to attract other businesses, describes himself as a salesman for the district, and opposes what he calls job-killing overregulation.
economy.short: Wants to grow regional energy sector; opposes overregulation.

taxes.summary: Voted for the $50.8 billion 2026-27 state budget, saying it includes no tax increases, comes in nearly $2.5 billion below the governor's original request, and leaves the Rainy Day Fund untouched.
taxes.short: Voted for 2026-27 budget; cites no tax increases.

abortion.summary: Voted for SB 106 in 2022, a proposed state constitutional amendment stating there is no right to abortion in Pennsylvania, and sponsored and voted for bills to prohibit abortions sought because of a prenatal Down syndrome diagnosis; his campaign site describes him as pro-life.
abortion.short: Voted for no-right-to-abortion amendment; describes himself pro-life.

education.summary: His campaign says a one-size-fits-all approach to education will not work and supports giving students and parents more choice in talent development, along with expanded education in STEM fields.
education.short: Supports more school choice for parents; expanded STEM education.

energy.summary: Opposes Pennsylvania's participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, which he calls a carbon tax that would raise prices and eliminate jobs, and praised its removal in the state budget; supports developing the state's natural gas resources to keep Pennsylvania a top energy exporter.
energy.short: Opposes RGGI carbon pricing; supports natural gas development.

guns.summary: His campaign site describes him as pro-Second Amendment and says he is committed to fighting the opioid epidemic; the site does not detail specific gun legislation.
guns.short: Describes himself pro-Second Amendment; commits to fighting opioids.

economy.summary: Her platform supports housing assistance programs including first-time homebuyer initiatives, minimum wage increases, paid family and sick leave, affordable childcare initiatives, and business partnerships to create career training and living-wage jobs.
economy.short: Supports housing assistance, minimum wage increase, paid leave, childcare.

taxes.summary: Her platform supports local tax relief for working families and seniors as part of an affordable-living agenda; the site does not detail broader state tax or budget positions.
taxes.short: Supports local tax relief for working families and seniors.

abortion.summary: Her platform says she will defend access to safe abortion services and reproductive health clinics, increase reproductive health education in schools, and support nonprofits providing resources for women and families.
abortion.short: Says she will defend abortion access and reproductive clinics.

education.summary: Her platform advocates increased state funding for public schools, manageable class sizes, expanded mental health services in schools, and partnerships with businesses and universities for mentorships and internships.
education.short: Advocates increased public school funding, smaller classes, mental health services.

healthcare.summary: Her platform proposes expanding Medicaid and prescription assistance programs, increasing funding for community health centers in underserved areas, and promoting policies that reduce surprise medical bills and improve transparency.
healthcare.short: Proposes expanding Medicaid, community health centers, reducing surprise bills.

energy.summary: Her platform supports renewable energy projects to reduce pollution, enforcing clean water and air standards, and strengthening zoning and environmental review standards for data centers so energy and water impacts are assessed before industrial projects are approved.
energy.short: Supports renewable energy, clean air standards, data center review.
